tob-10017: Job, the eighteenth book of the King James Bible, tells of a righteous man who loses everything — his wealth, his children, his health — and demands to know why God let it happen. His friends argue he must have sinned, but Job refuses their easy answers. It is the Bible’s deepest meditation on suffering and one of the oldest works of world literature.
tob-10817: Israel Abrahams traces the story of Jewish writing from the Bible’s closing books through two millennia of exile. His chapters cover the Talmud, medieval Hebrew poetry, the philosophers of Spain, and the Yiddish literature of his own day. Written with warmth and learning, the book shows a people’s literature as the record of its survival.
tob-4017: Vasari’s third volume rounds out his trail-blazing history of Italian art, covering the later masters and his own peers. He writes of Titian, Tintoretto, and the painters of his own time with an insider’s eye. The three volumes together form the founding text of art history, still read for pleasure as much as study.
tob-0117: James Anderson’s 1723 Constitutions is the ground-deed of ordered Freemasonry — its story, charges, and by-laws for London’s new Grand Lodge. The book fixed what a Mason is and how lodges go. Every Mason’s rule-book since stems from it.
tob-4117: The second volume of Kunjalal’s Sushruta Samhita carries on the old wound-classic — sicknesses, their cures, and the cutter’s art at large. The text shows Indian leechcraft at its ripest, ages ahead of its day. The pair keep a two-thousand-year-old healing lore.
cia-0000107417: A May 1981 Africa review examining the state of relations between apartheid South Africa and Israel. The two countries, both diplomatically isolated, had built a quiet partnership in trade and military technology. The document shows the CIA tracking an alliance that embarrassed both governments and worried their neighbors.
cia-0000119717: An estimated 1956 record of the CIA director dictating notes on an October 26 National Security Council meeting about Poland — the truncated title suggests Hungary too. Dictated summaries captured what the director thought mattered most. The entry is decision-making preserved in the director's own framing.
cia-0000124317: A July 1951 report on American prisoners of war in Communist China — the country-wide picture. Hundreds of Americans were held across China, many of them airmen. The document pulls the scattered reports into one grim survey.
cia-0000132617: Item 1 in the July 1960 general series: Bonn anticipating Cuban recognition of East Germany. West Germany watched Havana's diplomacy for the Hallstein tripwire. The document is the anticipation: the recognition, expected.
cia-0000135917: A 1954 routing sheet with an attached report on the K-program — subject deleted — covering the first meeting. The program's opening session, documented. The entry is the beginning: the first meeting, reported.
cia-0000136117: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting a newscast from Guatemala City radio — the archive's spelling says Guatamala — the truncated title cuts off the subject. The enemy's airwaves, monitored. The entry is the broadcast: the newscast, noted.
cia-0000136217: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for CADICK requesting a daily operations situation report. The tempo quickened: daily, not weekly. The document is the quickening: the reports, daily.
cia-0000136917: A 1954 cable to the senior representative in Guatemala City on the Washington Post and New York Times siding — the truncated title cuts off with whom. The press took sides. The document is the coverage: the papers, leaning.
cia-0000137317: The record of the 412th NSC meeting on July 23, 1959, with an attached NSC briefing — the truncated title cuts off the subject. A week after the 411th, the council met again. The document is the meeting: the 412th, following fast.
un-ga-res-17: UN General Assembly Resolution 17, dating to 1946. The founders voted; the record kept their numbers. The entry is the trace: the seventeenth act of the Assembly.
un-ga-res-a-69-17: Resolution A/69/17, adopted in 2016 — the session's business spilling into the next calendar year. The designation and year are preserved; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-17: Security Council Resolution 17, adopted in 1947. The Council's second year. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-217: Security Council Resolution 217, cataloged with the year 1961 — though the famous Rhodesia sanctions resolution 217 belongs to November 1965, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted — and the subject is left to the text.
un-sc-res-317: Security Council Resolution 317, adopted in 1972. The early-seventies Council deliberated. The designation and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-817: Security Council Resolution 817, adopted in April 1993 — the Macedonia admission resolution, recommending the former Yugoslav republic join the UN under the provisional name FYROM. The name dispute with Greece began here. The resolution is the compromise: the name, provisional.
un-sc-res-1317: Security Council Resolution 1317, adopted in 2000 — aligned. The Council's business rolled on. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1717: Security Council Resolution 1717, cataloged with the year 2008 — the numbering suggests 2006, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1817: Security Council Resolution 1817, cataloged with the year 1999 — the numbering suggests 2008, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
cia-0000135717: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135717. The exiles' own words, archived. The document is the archive: the words, theirs.
cia-0000136717: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136717. The invasion year's firm-dated papers. The entry is the firmness: the year, certain.
plos-pone-0000017: A 2006 PLOS ONE study: multilocus sequence typing breathes life into a microbial metagenome. A DNA-fingerprinting method makes sense of the microbial soup in an environmental sample. The paper is the method: the soup, sorted.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d17: The president's personal representative Harriman to the president — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 17. The envoy in Moscow reported home. The cable is the envoy's: Harriman, briefing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d117: The ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, to the President, November 12 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 117. Moscow's embassy reported. The cable is the embassy's: Harriman, briefing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d217: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 13, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 217. London wrote. The message is the letter: the prime minister, to the president.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d317: The Secretary of State to the President, November 25, 1943 — Document 317. The department's Thanksgiving briefing. The memo is the briefing: the secretary, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d417: The ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, to the Secretary of State — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 417. Another cable to the department. The cable is the second: Harriman, again.
arxiv-2605-08817: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards — RLVR — teaches models to reason, but they explore timidly. Yifan Xu, Junren Chen, and Yifan Chen show that the opening of the reasoning trace sets the tone: prefix-tuned priors steer the model toward bolder exploration from the first tokens. The 2026 paper is about getting language models to reason more adventurously.
arxiv-2605-08917: Bright meteors — fireballs — flash without warning, and catching them takes cameras watching the whole sky. M. Caldas, A. Guaimare, V. Abraham, and colleagues describe BOCOSUR, an all-sky camera network for fireball detection across Uruguay. The 2026 paper is observational-astronomy infrastructure for the Southern Hemisphere.
arxiv-2605-09017: Does this network contain a path — or a cycle — that visits certain nodes? Arjan Cornelissen, Amin Shiraz Gilani, and Subhasree Patro design quantum algorithms for these containment problems. The 2026 paper brings quantum computing to these classic questions in graph complexity theory.
arxiv-2605-09317: GUI agents click through software like humans — but they forget what they did three screens ago. The LV-NUS Lab proposes Mem-W: latent memory-native GUI agents that carry their history with them. The 2026 paper gives computer-using AI a working memory.
arxiv-2605-09617: Sudoku's innocent rules hide deep mathematics, and perfect error-correcting codes can generate symmetric Sudoku-type games. Junmin An, Jae-Hyun Baek, Keon-Hwi Kim, and colleagues build such games directly from codes. The 2026 paper is playful recreational mathematics with deep coding-theory roots.
arxiv-2605-09717: Conditional density estimation — predicting full probability distributions rather than just means — is a demanding statistical task needing regularization done right. Gilles Germain applies a general regularisation scheme to the problem. The 2026 paper is careful statistical methodology with genuinely wide applicability.
plos-pone-0003417: Clinicians compared TB tests head-to-head in this 2008 multicenter study. Interferon-gamma release assays had improved diagnosis of latent tuberculosis, but the team wanted to know how well single versus combined immune tests detect active disease. Testing patients across European centers, they measured the accuracy trade-offs, guiding which test combinations doctors should trust.
plos-pone-0003517: Developmental biologists mapped a signal sculpting the brain's dopamine heartland in this 2008 mouse study. Wnt5a, acting through the planar cell polarity pathway that orients cells, guides formation of the ventral midbrain and the A9-A10 dopamine neurons. Since those cells die in Parkinson's disease, their construction manual matters deeply.
plos-pone-0003617: Oncologists Rizzi, Belloni, and Crafa proposed a molecular fingerprint for prostate cancer in this 2008 paper. Their gene signature, read by RT-qPCR, aimed to improve on PSA screening's notorious false alarms. A reliable expression panel could catch curable prostate tumors earlier while sparing healthy men unnecessary biopsies.
plos-pone-0003717: In 2008, Erlich, Fry, and Begley tied a gene-reading helper to DNA repair. Yeast missing Anc1, a protein that rides along with transcription complexes, proved sensitive to DNA-damaging agents. The repair defect shows Anc1 moonlights beyond gene reading, guarding the genome after replication.
plos-pone-0003817: Clements, Gaboriaud, and Duval mapped the sugary armor of a lung pathogen in this 2008 paper. The surface saccharides of Klebsiella pneumoniae proved key to how the bacterium associates with host cells. The sugar coat is both shield and handshake in infection.
plos-pone-0003917: In 2008, Ahn, Byun, and Kim steered brain stem cells with a single gene. Switching on Olig2 pushed neural stem cells to differentiate, turning down Wnt signaling along the way. The Olig2 route reveals a control lever for making specific brain cells. The lever matters for both stem-cell therapies and brain tumor research.
plos-pone-0004017: In 2008, Saaf, Tengvall-Linder, and Chang profiled the genes of itchy skin. Atopic eczema skin showed inflammatory genes turned up and lipid genes turned down. The reciprocal expression pattern points to a broken skin-barrier program in patients. The global gene profile reframes eczema as barrier failure plus immune inflammation.
plos-pone-0004117: In 2009, Ellenbogen, Hulbert, and Jiang showed sleep guarding memory overnight. The sleeping brain's hard work boosted verbal memory's resistance to interference. Rest after learning shielded fresh words from competing noise. The neat study firms up sleep's role in memory consolidation.
plos-pone-0004217: In 2009, Finn, Tregenza, and Norman watched dolphins cook with their flippers. Dolphins showed complex prey handling while preparing cuttlefish meals. The marine mammals tenderized cuttlefish before eating. The underwater footage reveals dolphin food craft. The behavior shows culture-like learning at sea.
plos-pone-0004317: In 2009, White, Lewallen, and Beare read malaria in children's eyes. Retinal signs in Malawian children with cerebral malaria predicted coma and death. The eye exam became a prognostic tool. The findings sharpen bedside triage. The work validates retinopathy as a malaria severity marker.
plos-pone-0329717: Radiotherapy can paradoxically spur cancer invasion — and something in blood plasma carries the signal. This paper showed the Rab4A protein drives the enhancement of cancer cell invasion induced by plasma collected during radiotherapy from triple-negative breast cancer patients. Blocking Rab4A could stop treatment from backfiring on the very patients it aims to save.
plos-pone-0355417: Orthopaedic surgery remains one of medicine’s least diverse specialties. This paper asked where diversity currently stands in orthopaedic surgery residency applications. The numbers show honestly how far the pipeline has come — and how far it still has to go.
plos-pone-0356617: Lithium’s isotopes behave subtly differently in radical-pair reactions — quantum details with real consequences. This paper studied lithium isotope effects and magnetic interactions in flavin–ascorbyl radical pairs. The findings matter for understanding lithium’s biological and medical effects at the most fundamental level.
plos-pone-0357117: GP practices across the UK are morphing into team-based, multiprofessional care centers. The PRIMA study protocol plans a multicenter non-randomized study of this transformation, focusing on the role of nursing professionals. The planned research will map how the transition actually works in practice.
plos-pone-0357917: Serious disease reshapes lives long before diagnosis — and long after treatment ends. This paper traced long-term comparative trajectories of health, behavioral, and economic outcomes from pre-diagnosis through survivorship. The life-course view reveals the full arc of illness, far beyond the clinic’s narrow window.
plos-pone-0356917: Critically ill children on prolonged opioids face brutal withdrawal when the drugs stop. This paper supported clinical guidelines for opioid conversion to methadone and careful tapering, using physiology-based pharmacokinetic modeling. The models make the tapering process safer for the smallest, most vulnerable patients.
plos-pone-0354517: ‘My dog is my life’ — for homeless people, the bond with a companion animal runs profoundly deep. This paper applied One Health approaches to healthcare for homeless people and their dogs in the United Kingdom. The integrated approach treats human and animal health together, refusing to separate what life has joined.
plos-pone-0348517: Plant compounds might do double duty against flu and human metapneumovirus. This paper repositioned antiviral phytoconstituents as broad-spectrum inhibitors of influenza A neuraminidase and HMPV fusion protein. The natural molecules emerge as promising drug leads against two major respiratory threats.
plos-pone-0356817: Etching silicon precisely is the foundation of the entire semiconductor industry. This paper studied the etching characteristics and profile simulation of silicon. The detailed etch science helps chipmakers carve ever-smaller features with confidence.
plos-pone-0357017: Normalizing muscle mass by height squared creates a paradox that misclassifies patients. This population-based cross-sectional study showed the appendicular-to-trunk lean mass ratio resolves that paradox in low muscle mass and metabolic syndrome. The better ratio gives clinicians a more honest measure of who’s truly at risk.
plos-pone-0355717: Liver cancer’s driver mutations differ between populations — and Chinese patients were understudied. This paper examined driver mutation impact in Chinese hepatocellular carcinoma. The population-specific findings refine which mutations matter most, guiding targeted therapy choices for the world’s largest liver cancer burden.
plos-pone-0354817: Immunoglobulin is a precious, expensive therapy — and Canadian physicians must manage it wisely. This qualitative study explored how they do so. The candid physician perspectives reveal the bedside rationing, stewardship pressures, and ethical tensions behind every infusion decision. The findings inform national supply policy.
plos-pone-0354917: Counting insects in light traps over seasons and years reveals population rhythms invisible in snapshots. This paper analyzed seasonal and long-term population dynamics for modeling low-density populations, drawing on light trap experience. The methodological insights help ecologists detect the faint signals of declining insect populations before they vanish.
plos-pone-0353017: Mass coral bleaching and Cyclone Megan battered the Groote Archipelago’s reefs — and baselines were urgently needed. This paper established benthic baselines for the archipelago’s key reefs in the disaster’s wake. The baseline surveys are the reference point against which all future recovery — or further decline — will be measured.
plos-pone-0355117: Septic shock kills through cascading organ failure — but an unlikely drug combination might help. This paper showed vitamin B12 combined with methylene blue alleviates experimental septic shock, modulating KCNMB1 and the cGMP-PRKG pathway. The repurposed combination offers a cheap, accessible hope for intensive care.
europmc-pmc2831917: Nonstick and stain-guard chemicals are in nearly everyone's blood. This 2010 study ties contact with these long-lived compounds to higher cholesterol, weight, and insulin trouble in U.S. adults. The team mined a national health survey. The links raised alarms over compounds once thought harmless.
europmc-pmc2846417: Muscles repair themselves with stem cells that can wait quietly for years. This 2010 paper shows the protein Sprouty1 regulates the reversible quiescence of a self-renewing adult muscle stem cell pool during regeneration. The authors reveal the switch between dormancy and action. The finding matters for keeping muscle repair working with age.
europmc-pmc2869317: DNA differences that tune gene activity abound in the human brain. This 2010 paper finds many quantitative trait loci for DNA methylation and gene expression in brain tissue. The authors' haul links variants to brain function. Their data became a resource for neurogenetics.
europmc-pmc2893117: Beta-thalassemia, a blood disorder from faulty hemoglobin genes, burdens the Mediterranean and Asia. This 2010 review covers its forms, genetics, and care, from mild to severe. The authors distill guidance for a common inherited disease. Their review serves clinics worldwide that treat it.
europmc-pmc2893517: Gauging disability across diseases needs a trusted tool. This 2010 paper tests the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule, WHODAS-2, in people with long-term diseases. The authors confirm it works beyond single conditions. Their testing spread a standard yardstick for disability worldwide.
europmc-pmc2914717: Heat waves kill, and this 2010 paper counts the toll across nine European cities. The authors report the EuroHEAT project's findings on how heat waves drive mortality. Their city-by-city data reveals who is most at risk. The work shaped heat-health warning systems across Europe.
europmc-pmc2954317: Stem cells' birth can be watched one cell at a time. This 2010 paper traces embryonic stem cell derivation from the inner cell mass with single-cell RNA-Seq. The authors' pioneering method revealed early decisions. Their work launched single-cell genomics.
europmc-pmc2972217: The cell's fuel gauge talks to its recycling system. This 2010 paper shows AMPK's association with ULK1 regulates autophagy. The authors link energy sensing to self-eating. Their work connects metabolism to cellular housekeeping. Starved cells lean on this switch hard.
europmc-pmc3009617: Fabry disease starves cells of a key enzyme. This 2010 review covers Fabry disease, a rare inherited storage disorder. The author surveys its signs and care. Their overview aids diagnosis and treatment. Enzyme infusions now ease the burden. Gene therapy trials are underway.
europmc-pmc3071317: SARS survivors ached long after recovery. This 2011 study finds lasting pain, fatigue, low mood, and broken sleep after SARS. The authors' careful comparison documents the burden. Their work foreshadowed long COVID. Many never returned to full work. The pattern repeats in long COVID clinics.
europmc-pmc3091517: Cancer growth wiring got mapped. This 2011 review charts two master pathways behind growth, drug response, and aging. The authors' map guides cancer doctors. Their overview shaped drug combos. Blocking both paths beats blocking one. The map hangs in oncology labs.
europmc-pmc6538217: Astrocytes - the brain's star-shaped support cells - turn reactive in neurodegenerative disease, changing shape and behavior. This review examines that transformation: reactive astrocytes can shield neurons or, when overactivated, fuel inflammation and harm them. Understanding which state dominates in Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and ALS could unlock therapies that nudge these cells toward protection.
europmc-pmc6547017: When study data have holes, researchers often fill them with multiple imputation - but should the share of missing data decide? This paper says no: the proportion missing is a poor guide for choosing between imputation and analyzing complete cases. Using simulations and real examples, the authors give better rules for handling gaps without fooling yourself.
europmc-pmc6562917: Nanoparticles can ferry drugs to tumors - but only if they find the address. Coating the particles with biological ligands, molecules that home in on diseased cells, gives them a mailing address. This review surveys ligand-guided targeting strategies: which biological keys unlock which cellular doors, and how to build smarter delivery vehicles.
europmc-pmc6566317: Probiotics are usually sold alive - but live microbes can cause infections in fragile patients. Heat-killed (Tyndallized) probiotics offer a safer swap: dead bacteria that still nudge the immune system. This overview weighs the health benefits of inactivated probiotics, from gut calm to immune tuning, and where the evidence is strongest.
europmc-pmc6598417: AI tutors, virtual patients, and automated grading are entering medical schools - but the path is bumpy. This integrative review maps where artificial intelligence fits in medical education and what stands in the way: faculty readiness, ethics, and proof it works. The authors call for thoughtful adoption over hype-driven rollout.
europmc-pmc6637517: Two common antibiotics - ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin - moonlight as brain-inflammation dampeners. In lab models, the drugs quieted overactive microglia through the TLR4/NF-kB pathway. The finding suggests these familiar pills might be repurposed against neuroinflammatory disease.
europmc-pmc6642117: Macrophages depend on the CSF1R receptor - and a distant DNA switch, the FIRE enhancer, controls it. Deleting that enhancer in mice selectively throttled CSF1R and stunted tissue macrophage development. The experiment proves a faraway enhancer can be a master dial for immune cell populations.
europmc-pmc6647117: Frontotemporal dementia - which steals personality and language rather than memory - runs strongly in families. This update covers its genetics: the dominant mutations behind most inherited cases and how they shape disease. Understanding the genes guides diagnosis, counseling, and the hunt for treatments.
europmc-pmc6669617: H9N2 bird flu has quietly spread through poultry worldwide for two decades - mild in birds, but a pandemic wildcard. This global perspective reviews its march: high rates of jump to humans and a knack for swapping genes with deadlier flus. The mild virus deserves serious watching.
europmc-pmc6697717: Parkinson's arises from a conspiracy: aging, genes, and environment all push toward the same cliff. This review examines their interplay - how misfolded alpha-synuclein spreads, Lewy bodies form, and dopamine neurons die. No single cause explains the disease; the review maps how the culprits collaborate.
europmc-pmc6715717: The brain's repair crew - oligodendrocyte precursor cells - may moonlight as immune informants. In inflammatory demyelination, these precursors present antigens and become targets for killer cells, sabotaging myelin repair. The study reveals why remyelination stalls in multiple sclerosis - and where to intervene.
europmc-pmc6753017: Cancer kills millions yearly - and the old weapons are not enough. This review tours innovative treatment approaches: the new ideas in the pipeline and the hurdles they face. The field's creativity is its best asset against a shape-shifting foe.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-17: This 2007 Government Accountability Office report found that thousands of health care providers enrolled in Medicaid were abusing the federal tax system — collecting government health payments while owing large unpaid tax debts. Investigators matched provider records against tax data to expose the pattern. The report raises an uncomfortable question: should programs that pay with taxpayer money do business with tax cheats?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1117: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report on end-stage renal disease: who receives kidney transplants, how often transplants fail, and what the program costs Medicare. Kidney failure treatment is one of Medicare's most expensive commitments. GAO's analysis gives Congress data on outcomes and spending for a program where the government is effectively the insurer of last resort.
gao-gaoreports-b-299817: S4, Inc. doubled down on its 2007 protest — two case numbers, one fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. The firm said the agency's award was flawed; the call tests each claim to the finish. Persistence in the protest game gets one consolidated answer.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-917: New rail lines were queuing up in 2007 — GAO's report says demand for transit-building grants would grow, but the grant machinery needed fixing. The findings pair a transit boom forecast with a bureaucratic tune-up list. The report bets on trains while demanding better tracks for the money.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-717: The mail's big reshuffle needed explaining in 2007 — GAO's report says the Postal Service's processing realignment wanted better integration and plainer talk. The findings press for a coherent story. The report's demand: tell the public what the new mail map means.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-817: Other nations were doing better by women and low-skill workers in 2007 — GAO's report shops the globe for policies that helped them land and keep jobs. The findings import ideas worth stealing. The report's pitch: the best labor policy may already exist somewhere else.
gao-gaoreports-b-299517: Sumaria Systems doubled its June 2007 protest — two case numbers, one tech fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims. The firm challenged the awards as unfair; the call weighs each claim to a close. Paired filings get a paired answer from the referee.
gao-gaoreports-b-299317: L-3 Communications Titan tripled its March 2007 protest — three case numbers, one defense-tech fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles all three claims. The firm challenged the awards; the call weighs each claim with care. Triple filings get one triple-checked answer.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-17: The GSA's broker experiment needed work in 2007, and GAO's report says the early rollout of the national broker contracts showed gaps. The findings flag the flaws. The report warns that the government's landlord should not lease blind. The deals needed daylight.
pmc-13516917: A 2026 computational biology paper introducing AbAgKer, a semi-supervised learning framework that predicts how strongly and how quickly antibodies bind their targets. Antigen-antibody affinity and kinetics are central to vaccine and drug design, and the tool aims to make those predictions from far less labeled data. It could speed up early-stage antibody screening.
pmc-13463317: This 2026 cardiology paper measures how common kinesiophobia — fear of movement after a heart procedure — is among patients who had percutaneous coronary intervention, the stent procedure for blocked arteries. The multicenter study also looks at what factors raise the risk. Naming the fear is the first step to getting recovering patients moving again.
pmc-13444717: In this 2026 Alzheimer's genetics paper, researchers used a polygenic risk score — a combined measure of many common genetic variants — to stratify patients, which helped uncover rare variants that would otherwise stay hidden. Common and rare genetics reinforce each other. The strategy could sharpen risk prediction and gene discovery.
pmc-13441517: A 2026 randomized study testing whether online attachment priming plus mindfulness practice eases insomnia, stress, and emotion dysregulation in university students. The intervention is fully digital — brief exercises delivered online. Positive results would mean a scalable, low-cost mental health tool for campuses.
pmc-13466717: A 2026 multinational real-world study of sacituzumab govitecan — an antibody-drug conjugate — in older patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Older patients are underrepresented in trials, so real-world data fills the gap. The study reports how the drug performed in this group.
pmc-13348017: A 2026 qualitative study asking traumatic brain injury survivors how it feels to be helped with minimal cognitive assistance. The lightest touch of help preserves dignity and autonomy. The first-person accounts reframe rehabilitation around the recipient's experience.
pmc-13484517: This 2026 cross-national study examined mortality among older Hispanic adults carrying the dual burdens of diabetes and dementia. The intersection of the two diseases compounds risk. The cross-national evidence highlights a vulnerable population.
pmc-13457917: A 2026 Tromsø Study analysis of atrial fibrillation and heart attack risk by sex and time since diagnosis, spanning 1994–2021. The decades-long Norwegian cohort gives rare long-term data. The sex-specific patterns inform risk counseling.
pmc-13488317: A 2026 review of diversity within ovarian cancer subtypes and their tumor microenvironment. Ovarian cancer isn't one disease. The review maps the subtypes and their immune landscapes.
pmc-13521017: This 2026 research note described colorimetric phenotyping of bruises in broiler carcasses under commercial slaughterhouse conditions. Bruise color indicates age and cause. The method serves poultry welfare auditing.
pmc-13467917: This 2026 review framed left ventricular diastolic dysfunction as the missing window for early intervention in diabetic cardiomyopathy. Catching the stiff heart early could change outcomes. The paper argues for the overlooked opportunity.
pmc-13453017: This 2026 cardiology paper identified predictors of echocardiographic abnormalities in asymptomatic people with an enlarged cardiothoracic ratio on chest X-ray. The big heart shadow needs triage. The predictors guide who needs an echo.
pmc-13561517: In this 2026 bioinformatics paper, MultiDMPcaller — a one-stop software — detected and visualized differentially methylated positions and regions. The tool simplifies methylation analysis. The software is the deliverable.
pmc-13531617: This 2026 cardiology commentary addressed warfarin, low-risk clusters, and resource-limited settings. The old anticoagulant's role was reconsidered. The commentary is the perspective.
pmc-13495117: This 2026 paper developed CanDi-Score — a candidaemia score for deciding early empirical antifungal treatment in ICU patients (the title is truncated). The score guides the antifungal call. The development is the clinical tool.
pmc-13579217: This 2026 catalysis paper escaped the scaling relationships in oxygen reduction catalysis — implications for PEM fuel cells. The fundamental limit was broken. The escaping is the breakthrough.
pmc-13450417: A 2026 chemistry paper on dynamics of (hetero)aryl motifs — an integrative approach to the conformational landscape in macrocycles. The ring conformations were mapped. The approach is the method.
pmc-13505517: In this 2026 policy paper, Medicaid payment policies for methadone maintenance treatment for opioid use disorder were tracked from 2020 to 2025. The payment landscape was mapped. The policies affect access.
pmc-13428217: In this 2026 paper, machine learning and SHAP values unraveled serum zinc levels' impact on chronic kidney disease. The zinc-kidney link was interpreted. The unraveling is the AI insight.
pmc-13446717: This 2026 corrigendum amended a paper on circulating microRNA profiles and identification of miR-593 and miR-511 targeting the PROP1 gene in children with combined pituitary hormone deficiency (the title is truncated). Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the corrigendum.
pmc-13509217: A 2026 ophthalmology paper: repeated prophylactic antimicrobial eye drop use was associated with reduced antimicrobial susceptibility in conjunctival and nasal commensal bacteria (the title is truncated). The eye drops bred resistance. The association is the warning.
pmc-13465117: A 2026 paper: ferroptosis inducers combined with copper ionophores aggravated lung cancer-related fatigue via GSH depletion and FKBP5-associated Nrf2/HO-1 impairment (the title is truncated). The drug combo worsened the fatigue. The aggravating is the mechanistic warning.
pmc-13470317: A 2026 labor economics paper: "More than mirror images" — health associations of transitions between formal and informal employment. The job transitions' health effects were mapped. The associations are the finding.
pmc-13470117: A 2026 case report of recurrent aqueous misdirection following intraluminal ripcord removal from a Paul glaucoma implant. The eye pressure crisis recurred. The case warns glaucoma surgeons.
pmc-13463117: A 2026 obstetrics paper: myometrial mechanotransduction and the timing of parturition — ion-channel pathways linking uterine stretch, calcium signaling, and inflammation. The labor trigger was mechanistically explained. The linking is the physiology.
pmc-13461317: A 2026 Vancouver cross-sectional study of nutrition knowledge among adolescent athletes. The young athletes' nutrition literacy was measured. The knowledge gaps inform coaching.
pmc-13424517: A 2026 stroke paper: cerebral small vessel disease impaired dynamic cerebral autoregulation and mediated outcomes after stroke thrombectomy. The small vessels' dysfunction worsened the thrombectomy results. The mediating is the mechanism.
pmc-13421117: In this 2026 prospective study, short-term efficacy and safety of 5MHz fractional microneedle radiofrequency for facial rejuvenation were tested. The skin treatment worked. The testing is the aesthetic evidence.
arxiv-2606-16517: AI models trained on biology can reason about genes, proteins, and pathways — but post-training (fine-tuning, RLHF) reshapes them in poorly understood ways. This paper studies how post-training shapes biological reasoning models. It targets researchers building AI for science who need to know what fine-tuning does to scientific competence.
arxiv-2606-16717: Drones watching the ocean need to beam data home without wasting power. This paper uses sensing-assisted predictive beamforming: the drone predicts where to aim its radio beam for UAV-enabled ocean monitoring networks. It is for wireless engineers working on ocean drones.
